title: Larger PDFs and audio fit into chat requests
summary:
Larger inline media, more capable account tools, and a crop of Jev-powered community projects.

Chat requests over 32 MiB can now carry inline PDF data for OpenRouter models and base64 audio for `thinkingmachines/inkling`. The gateway handles the large media without requiring callers to change their requests, and the API docs now spell out the per-item and post-replacement limits.

Six MCP tools add usage history, earnings, Quest status, and API-key management for agents with the relevant permissions. The polli 0.1.23 release also includes the previously merged sandbox create, list, kill, and SSH-config commands.

Quest contributors added three reviewable code agents: a context trimmer that selects archived outputs before answering, a Nomic rule voter that explains its verdict, and Cerberus, which chooses a security-triage playbook. Publishing access expanded for five community contributors; the merged agent code does not establish that each agent is publicly callable.

highlights.title: Larger inline chat media
highlights.text: Send inline PDFs in chat requests to OpenRouter models, or base64 audio to `thinkingmachines/inkling`, even when the request exceeds 32 MiB. Individual media items remain limited to 20 MiB. [Read the API docs](https://gen.pollinations.ai/docs).

highlights.title: Account tools for MCP
highlights.text: MCP agents can check usage, earnings, and Quest status, or list, create, and revoke API keys when granted the relevant permissions. [Explore the MCP docs](https://gen.pollinations.ai/docs#tag/mcp-servers).

highlights.title: Sandbox commands in polli
highlights.text: `polli` 0.1.23 includes commands to create, list, and kill sandboxes, plus `ssh-config` for connecting to them. [Find the CLI package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@pollinations/cli).

highlights.title: Jev context-trimmer agent
highlights.text: Explore a community code agent that uses Jev to select relevant archived outputs before GPT-5.4 Nano answers, and returns what it kept alongside the answer. Its example shows how to deploy and call the owner-accessible agent through `/v1/responses`. [Browse the code](https://github.com/pollinations/pollinations).

highlights.title: Nomic Player code agent
highlights.text: Explore a community agent that asks Jev for a yes-or-no vote on a Nomic rule proposal, then generates an argument without changing the verdict. It returns the vote and probabilities through chat or responses inputs. [Browse the code](https://github.com/pollinations/pollinations).

highlights.title: Cerberus security-triage agent
highlights.text: Explore a community agent that maps a finding to a contain, investigate, or maintain playbook using Jev, then explains the choice. The code and setup example are available; public access to the agent is not established. [Browse the code](https://github.com/pollinations/pollinations).
